```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# clear environment so knitting only depends on what's in this file
rm(list = ls())

# installs (if missing) and loads every package this project uses - add any
# new packages to scripts/00-packages.R, not here
source("../scripts/00-packages.R")

# downloads the data into data/raw/ if you don't already have it, then loads
# eindscores, referentieniveaus, schooladviezen and schoolweging into this
source("../scripts/01-get-data.R")
```


```{r prepare-data}

#Select relevant reference-level variables
count_cols <- c("REKENEN_LAGER1F", "REKENEN_1F", "REKENEN_1S",
                "LV_LAGER1F", "LV_1F", "LV_2F")

# value for DUO's "<5" (1-4 pupils): the midpoint
lt5_value <- 2.5

replace_lt5 <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  as.numeric(if_else(x == "<5", as.character(lt5_value), x))
}

#Convert columns to numeric, and turn values like <5 to NA
#Clean reference-level counts
ref_levels <- referentieniveaus |>
  mutate(across(all_of(count_cols), replace_lt5)) |> #used to turn <5 into NA, now into 2.5 to prevent false 100$ scores? For small schools, this quite greatly influenced averages for example. 
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    GEMEENTENAAM = first(GEMEENTENAAM),
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING = first(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING),
    across(all_of(count_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    #total number of students for maths and for reading
    rekenen_n = REKENEN_LAGER1F + REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S,
    reading_n = LV_LAGER1F + LV_1F + LV_2F,
    #percentage of students for each level
    math_1F = 100 * (REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S) / rekenen_n,
    math_1S = 100 * REKENEN_1S / rekenen_n,
    reading_1F = 100 * (LV_1F + LV_2F) / reading_n,
    reading_2F = 100 * LV_2F / reading_n
    #DUO only count each pupil once, so to get the totals for reaching 1F in both reading and math, you must also count         the pupils that reached 1S and 2F
  ) |>
  filter(rekenen_n > 0, reading_n > 0)
    #filter out schools where no pupils are counted for maths and reading, this might not occur for Amstelveen, but is          necessary for calculating averages.

#calculate Schoolweging
school_weights <- schoolweging |>
  mutate(INSTELLINGSCODE = str_remove(OVT, "\\|.*$")) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(schoolweging = weighted.mean(schoolweging, w = aantal_leerlingen),
    .groups = "drop")

#Combine reference-level results with schoolweging
school_data <- left_join(ref_levels, school_weights, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE")

#Amstelveen Gemeente
amstelveen_data <- filter(school_data, GEMEENTENAAM == "Amstelveen")

#Final data
amstelveen_data |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, schoolweging,
          math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F)

```

```{r filter-converse}
# all Dutch schools, one row per school per level
final_data <- school_data |>
  filter(!is.na(schoolweging)) |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, GEMEENTENAAM, schoolweging,
         rekenen_n, reading_n,
         math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F),
    names_to = "level",
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    subject = if_else(str_starts(level, "math"), "Maths", "Reading"),
    type = if_else(str_ends(level, "1F"),
                   "Basic level (1F)",
                   "Target level (1S / 2F)"),
    n_students = if_else(subject == "Maths", rekenen_n, reading_n)
  )

#check if filter and conversion was succesful, are school with no schoolweging really filtered out and is nrow(final_data) x 4 times this amount
count(final_data, level, subject, type)
nrow(final_data)
```

```{r split-data-per-layer}
# grey background: all Dutch schools
# national <- final_data coded out, the grey dots were messy

# the municipality we highlight
municipality <- "Amstelveen"

muni_data <- final_data |>
  filter(GEMEENTENAAM == municipality) |>
  mutate(passed = if_else(percentage >= 85, "Yes", "No"))

# Amstelveen dots, split per row of the plot (each gets its own colours)
muni_1f <- filter(muni_data, type == "Basic level (1F)")
muni_target <- filter(muni_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# regression line: all Dutch schools, only the target levels
national_target <- filter(final_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# 85% norm line: one row per 1F panel
norm_1f <- distinct(muni_1f, type, subject)
```

```{r names-in-plot}
# names in the plot: all schools in the 1S / 2F panels, and only the
# schools below the 85% norm in the 1F panels
label_data <- muni_data |>
  filter(
    type == "Target level (1S / 2F)" |
      (type == "Basic level (1F)" & passed == "No")
  ) |>
  mutate(label = if_else(
    type == "Basic level (1F)",
    paste0(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, "\n", round(percentage, 2), "%"),
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING
  ))

# school name with its school weighting, for the y-axis
muni_target <- muni_target |>
  mutate(school_label = paste0(
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, " (SW ", round(schoolweging), ")"
  ))
```

```{r scatter-1f--plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
plot_1f <- ggplot(muni_1f, aes(x = schoolweging, y = percentage)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 85, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = passed, size = n_students),
             shape = 21, color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(label_data, type == "Basic level (1F)"),
                  aes(label = label), size = 3.5, lineheight = 0.9,
                  nudge_x = 1, nudge_y = -1, hjust = 0, direction = "y",
                  segment.color = NA, seed = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#009E73", "No" = "#B2182B"),
                    name = "Meets 85% norm") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, name = "Number of students") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 5))) +
  facet_wrap(~ subject) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Almost all schools in Amstelveen reach the basic reference",
      "level;\nonly two fall below the national signalling value."
    ),
    subtitle = paste(
      "90% of schools (n = 18) meet the 85% norm in both subjects,",
      "while 10% (n = 2) do not."
    ),
    x = "School weighting (higher = more disadvantaged pupils)",
    y = "% of pupils reaching 1F"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 18),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
plot_1f
```
